summary: Week 5 turns on quarterback absences: Mayfield and Caleb Williams are out, Lamar Jackson is reported unlikely and Jayden Daniels is questionable. The market keeps pricing records over efficiency, which creates value on Las Vegas, Chicago, the Giants, Tennessee and the Chargers, and many of the best angles are unders and team-total unders against broken offenses (Miami, New England, Green Bay, Philadelphia). Watch the line moves (the BAL-ATL spread flipped, the HOU-TEN total fell two points) and the injury tags: several reports treated questionable players such as Smith, Gonzalez, Jefferson, Allen, Cross and Benford as out. Early forecasts for wind at Lambeau and gusty rain in Pittsburgh are days out and only lean things further under.

picks.label: Spread
picks.case: Tampa's defense ranks 5th in EPA and 3rd against the run, and all four of its losses came by seven or fewer. Dallas has won only one of four by more than 4 points behind a defense ranked 31st overall and last against the pass. Four reports from both sides land here. The line has already dropped from 9.5 to 8.5, so a point of value is gone, but the case was built on a fair number near a touchdown.
picks.risk: Tampa's offense is 32nd in EPA and now without Mayfield and Winfield, so a Dallas air-raid rout (3rd in pass EPA) is very possible.

picks.label: Game total
picks.case: Dallas is 4-0 to the over, but those games came against more explosive offenses. Tampa brings the league's worst passing offense with a backup quarterback and a 5th-ranked defense, and its games average 43 combined points. Tampa's 3rd-ranked run defense takes away Dallas's ground game, which tends to turn drives into field goals.
picks.risk: Dallas's 31st-ranked defense, now missing Thompson and likely Overshown and Durant, could let even Daniels keep pace in a shootout.

picks.label: Daniels rushing yards
picks.case: His 32 average is dragged down by a 6%-snap cameo. As a full-time starter he ran 8 times for 55 yards, and a 17.5% scramble rate is a habit. Dallas ranks 19th against the run, will likely be without linebacker Overshown, and a trailing script means more dropbacks to scramble from.
picks.risk: One start is a thin baseline, and a quick-throw game plan could keep him in the pocket.

picks.label: Spread
picks.case: Jacksonville is 2nd in net EPA to Philadelphia's 31st, and both teams' and both quarterbacks' reports land on the Jaguars. Philadelphia's offense is 28th in EPA with Goedert doubtful and Barkley, Jurgens and Smith questionable, and its pass rush is 31st in pressure rate. Lane Johnson is now off the report and Smith is questionable rather than out, so the injury gap is a bit narrower than the reports assumed.
picks.risk: 7 is a key number, so a push or a late backdoor score helped by Philadelphia's 4th-ranked special teams is the classic way this fails.

picks.label: Team total
picks.case: The line implies about 17.75 for an offense that averaged 18.8 with a healthier lineup and ranks 30th in success rate. Jacksonville allows 13.3 points a game and 28.6% red-zone touchdowns, and it leads the league at +1.5 turnovers per game. Both teams' reports agree.
picks.risk: Jacksonville's defense leaks deep balls, and a garbage-time touchdown or a return score could carry Philadelphia past 17.

picks.label: Game total
picks.case: Jacksonville's games average about 39 combined points, with three of four under. Philadelphia passes 5.7% below expectation and ranks 30th in success rate. A Jaguars lead built on their 5th-ranked run game should drain the clock, and the early London forecast is benign.
picks.risk: Jacksonville's 7th-ranked offense could score 30 by itself against a defense 24th in EPA.

picks.bet: Hurts under his 1.75-a-game passing TD average
picks.label: Hurts passing TDs
picks.case: Jacksonville allows one passing TD a game to quarterbacks, second-fewest in the league, and ranks 6th in pass-defense EPA. His own rate rests on five red-zone scores from 13 attempts, and Goedert is doubtful with Smith questionable.
picks.risk: Trailing big, Hurts racks up attempts and finds two garbage-time scores.

picks.label: Spread
picks.case: The teams are nearly identical by net EPA (-0.087 vs -0.069), so 2.5 is roughly home field. The Colts' top-ranked rushing offense meets a run defense ranked 20th, and Pittsburgh's offense is 24th in EPA and 27th passing. The early forecast of rain and 30-mph gusts is far out, but if it holds it favors the run game and the points.
picks.risk: Indy's -1.5 turnover margin (31st) against a top-six takeaway defense, plus Pittsburgh's 10 days of rest, could decide it.

picks.label: Game total
picks.case: Both passing offenses sit near the bottom (Colts 30th, Steelers 27th in pass EPA), and Pittsburgh's games have averaged 41 combined points. Indy runs first with Allen questionable and Pierce on IR. The forecast of rain and gusts to 30 mph is days out, but it only pushes the same way.
picks.risk: Pittsburgh's leaky deep defense, or Colts giveaways that hand the Steelers short fields.

picks.label: Jones passing yards
picks.case: Pierce is on IR, Allen is questionable, and Pittsburgh is strong underneath, where Jones lives. The Colts' most efficient path is the league-best run game, and the gusty early forecast leans the same way.
picks.risk: Pittsburgh allows 238 passing yards a game to quarterbacks, and a trailing script would force Jones to throw.

picks.label: Spread
picks.case: Las Vegas is 5th in net EPA with a +7.8 point differential and the 2nd-ranked defense. New England is 16th at -3.0 per game and 30th in scoring at 16.3, yet the Raiders get more than a field goal. Four reports from both sides agree the line is pricing last year's Patriots. Gonzalez is questionable, not confirmed out.
picks.risk: The Raiders' 4-0 ATS run includes +1.42 wins over expected, and their 29th-ranked run game can stall if they fall behind.

picks.label: Team total
picks.case: The line implies about 24.5 for a Patriots offense averaging 16.3 that has topped that number once in four games, against the 29th-ranked defense. It faces the 2nd-ranked pressure rate (29.9%) and a defense 2nd in EPA, with Brown on IR and Hollins questionable.
picks.risk: The Raiders' red-zone defense ranks 29th, so a few short fields off Cousins interceptions could get New England there.

picks.label: Moneyline
picks.case: +160 implies about a 38% chance for the team with the better net EPA (5th vs 16th), point differential and pass rush. New England turns it over 1.3 times a game more than its opponents and faces the league's takeaway leader.
picks.risk: Cousins has thrown a pick in three of four games, and a turnover-driven home win is the obvious path for New England.

picks.label: Maye passing yards
picks.case: Las Vegas ranks 3rd in pass-defense EPA and 5th against deep throws, his most productive depth, and pressures at the 2nd-highest rate. Hollins is questionable and Brown is on IR.
picks.risk: A trailing script could give him enough attempts to clear it on volume alone.

picks.label: Spread
picks.case: The teams are within 0.016 in net EPA, so the line is basically home field, and Cleveland has 10 days of rest. The Jets list Hall, Taylor and Mitchell as doubtful, and Onyemata is on IR. The Jets' report calls Cleveland's 3-1 lucky, which is fair, but this price already treats the teams as even.
picks.risk: Cleveland's 31st-ranked run game and league-high penalty rate, with center Jenkins questionable, could stall an offense that has to throw everything.

picks.label: Watson completions
picks.case: Cleveland passes more than any team relative to situation (+7.2%). The Jets rank 27th against short passes and 30th in success rate allowed, exactly where Watson completes 78%.
picks.risk: A protection breakdown behind a backup center, or an early lead that lets Cleveland run, trims his attempts.

picks.bet: Geno Smith over his 3-a-game sacks taken
picks.label: Smith sacks taken
picks.case: He ranks 30th of 32 in pressure-to-sack rate, Cleveland's sack rate is 9th, and guard Parham is questionable. Losing Hall and Taylor also takes away his checkdown outlets.
picks.risk: Graham's MCL and ankle sprain could thin Cleveland's front, and a quick-game plan could keep him upright.

picks.label: Spread
picks.case: The teams are within 0.013 in net EPA, and the Giants hold a roughly 9-point-per-game special-teams edge over Washington's 28th-ranked unit. Daniels (dislocated elbow), McLaurin and Cosmi are questionable and Mariota is doubtful. The line moved from 3 to 3.5, which helps this side.
picks.risk: A fully healthy Daniels changes Washington's offense, and the Giants' 3-1 rests on a perfect one-score record that may not hold.

picks.label: Team sacks
picks.case: Washington's 6th-ranked pressure rate has produced only 7 sacks in four games. The Giants allow sacks on 8.7% of dropbacks, 27th, and have taken 11 already, so this is the spot for pressure to turn into sacks.
picks.risk: The Giants pass 10% below expectation (30th), so few dropbacks cap the chances, and Omenihu's groin injury could thin the rush.

picks.bet: Winston over his 1-a-game passing TD average
picks.label: Winston passing TDs
picks.case: Washington allows three passing TDs a game to quarterbacks (31st) and ranks 26th against deep passes, where his touchdowns come from. Safeties Cross and Reaves are both questionable (Cross isn't confirmed out, as the report assumed).
picks.risk: The Giants' run-heavy plan, plus a five-day-out forecast of showers, could keep his attempts low.

picks.label: Spread
picks.case: The league's top defense by EPA and pressure rate (37.9%) faces a Saints line that ranks 24th in pressure allowed. New Orleans is -1.3 per game in turnovers against Minnesota's +1.3. At 1.5 the Vikings essentially just need to win.
picks.risk: Minnesota's offense is 27th in EPA, now without Jackson and Oliver and with Jefferson and Darrisaw questionable, so it may not score enough to win.

picks.label: Game total
picks.case: Four reports agree. Minnesota's offense is last in success rate, passes 5% below expectation, and its defense allows 12.8 points a game with the league's lowest red-zone TD rate. The offense is thinner still with Jackson and Oliver on IR and Jefferson and Darrisaw questionable, and New Orleans is missing Etienne.
picks.risk: The Saints' 26th-ranked defense pushed three of their four games over, and Saints giveaways could hand Minnesota short fields.

picks.label: Shough sacks taken
picks.case: Minnesota leads the league in sack rate (10.5%) and pressure rate, and Shough turns 34.5% of pressures into sacks. He already took 12 sacks against weaker fronts.
picks.risk: A quick-game plan or heavy max protection could keep him at three or fewer.

picks.bet: Shough under his 2.25-a-game passing TD average
picks.label: Shough passing TDs
picks.case: Minnesota allows 0.75 passing TDs a game to quarterbacks, fewest in the league, and has the top pass defense by EPA. His own rate rests on an unsustainable 8 red-zone scores on 27 attempts.
picks.risk: Minnesota turnovers could hand him short fields where touchdowns come easily.

picks.label: Game total
picks.case: Four reports agree. Green Bay scores about 18.3 a game with the league's worst rushing EPA, and Chicago starts a backup quarterback while leading the league in possession time. Green Bay may be without center Monk and lost tackle Bako-Bewele. The early Lambeau forecast of 19-mph wind and 27-mph gusts is five days out, but it leans the same way.
picks.risk: Green Bay's leaky red-zone defense, or a deep shot against a thin Bears secondary.

picks.label: Team total
picks.case: Green Bay hasn't topped 22 points in any game. It faces the 2nd-ranked pass defense and 3rd-ranked pressure rate from a defense allowing 16.3 a game. Its line allows the most QB hits in the league and may be without center Monk.
picks.risk: A defensive or special-teams score, or Bears turnovers, could gift Green Bay cheap points.

picks.label: Spread
picks.case: Chicago is 4th in net EPA to Green Bay's 30th, and the Packers have a -8 per-game point differential with Cooper on IR. Chicago covered both of its backup-quarterback starts. The reports disagree on whether Bagent or Keenum starts, but either way it's a backup.
picks.risk: A field-goal-heavy backup offense makes 3 a fragile margin, and a push is very live.

picks.label: Love passing yards
picks.case: Chicago allows the third-fewest quarterback yards (210.3) and ranks 2nd in pass EPA. Love's average is inflated by 387- and 312-yard games in losing scripts, and the early wind forecast could help further.
picks.risk: If Green Bay falls behind, his volume climbs again, as it did in those two games.

picks.label: Team total
picks.case: Miami averages 11.5 points (32nd) and hasn't topped 13 in any game, yet the line implies about 17.75. Achane is on IR, and Cincinnati brings a top-two sack rate and the 3rd-stingiest red-zone defense against an offense 31st in success rate. Both teams' reports agree, and the forecast is fine.
picks.risk: A defensive score, or a short field off a Cincinnati turnover, could add a cheap touchdown.

picks.label: Game total
picks.case: Miami's games average 36.8 combined points with three of four under. Its offense supplies so little that Cincinnati would need to score close to 30 on its own, with Chase and Higgins both questionable.
picks.risk: Burrow against the 29th-ranked pass defense, especially if Chase plays.

picks.label: Willis sacks taken
picks.case: He has a 9.6% sack rate and a career-long habit of holding the ball, and he faces a Cincinnati defense near the top in sack rate (3.5 sacks a game). A likely trailing script forces more dropbacks behind a line 27th at preventing sacks.
picks.risk: His scrambles and run-heavy usage cut his dropbacks.

picks.bet: Willis one or fewer passing TDs
picks.label: Willis passing TDs
picks.case: He has 1 passing TD in four games and a -0.709 red-zone EPA. Cincinnati allows only 1.25 TDs a game to quarterbacks, 5th-fewest.
picks.risk: Garbage-time drives against soft coverage could produce a pair of late scores.

picks.label: Spread
picks.case: These teams are near-identical: -7.0 vs -6.3 point differential per game and -0.112 vs -0.094 net EPA, yet Houston lays more than a touchdown on the road while 0-4 ATS. Houston's 30th-ranked run game can't salt away a lead, and Tennessee's run-first plan shortens the game. The line moved from 7 to 7.5, adding a half-point.
picks.risk: Tennessee's 25th-ranked passing offense and league-worst special teams could hand Houston a margin.

picks.label: Stroud passing yards
picks.case: His average is propped up by trailing scripts, including 353 yards on 55 attempts. As a 7.5-point favorite against the league's most run-heavy offense, Houston should see fewer dropbacks, and Tennessee allows 238.8 yards a game to quarterbacks.
picks.risk: Tennessee's secondary ranks 31st in deep EPA, so a couple of deep shots could get him there anyway.

picks.label: Spread
picks.case: Denver is 20th in net EPA with a -5 point differential and a 2-0 one-score record, yet lays more than a field goal on the road. Surtain is doubtful and Moss questionable, and Denver's 31st-ranked run defense faces a run-first opponent whose defense ranks 11th. Three reports agree.
picks.risk: LA's offense is 30th in EPA, with Slater out and Alt, Penning and Awosika questionable, so it may not score enough to stay close.

picks.label: Game total
picks.case: Denver scores 18.5 a game and the Chargers 16.8. Three of Denver's four games went under, and the Chargers pass 9% below expectation, which shortens games. It's indoors, so the forecast doesn't matter.
picks.risk: Chargers turnovers handing Denver short fields, or Denver exploiting LA's 25th-ranked explosive-pass defense.

picks.label: Herbert rushing yards
picks.case: He scrambles on 9% of dropbacks behind a line that ranks last in hit rate and is now without Slater, facing a Denver rush 6th in hit rate. He ran for 40 yards in his most pressured game.
picks.risk: Pressure turns into sacks rather than scrambles, or a run-heavy plan cuts his dropbacks.

picks.label: Game total
picks.case: Detroit's defense is 32nd in EPA and 30th against the pass, and Arizona's pass defense is 31st. All four Detroit games went over, averaging about 61.5 points, and Arizona's last two hit 66 and 60. The wind-and-drizzle forecast shouldn't matter, since the retractable roof is likely closed.
picks.risk: The number is already very high, and Arizona's run game against Detroit's 29th-ranked run defense could drain the clock.

picks.bet: Goff over his 2.25-a-game passing TD average
picks.label: Goff passing TDs
picks.case: Arizona allows 2.75 passing TDs a game to quarterbacks (30th), and its 5th-ranked run defense pushes Detroit's red-zone work into the air, where Goff has 8 TDs on 34 attempts.
picks.risk: Detroit's backs punch in the short scores instead.

picks.label: Brissett passing yards
picks.case: Detroit allows a league-worst 350 yards a game to quarterbacks and is missing Ya-Sin and Harper in the secondary. A 54.5 total points to a shootout with Arizona trailing, the script that produced his 280-yard Week 3.
picks.risk: Without Paris Johnson, Arizona may lean on the run to control the clock rather than chase.

picks.label: Spread
picks.case: Detroit is only 18th in net EPA, about 0.045 per play ahead of Arizona, which with home field argues for a line near a field goal. Arizona's run game gets a 29th-ranked run defense, and Detroit's last-ranked defense has kept even its wins close.
picks.risk: Detroit's 4th-ranked passing game against Arizona's 31st-ranked pass defense could blow it open.

picks.label: Spread
picks.case: San Francisco's net EPA of 0.267 (1st) is more than double Seattle's 0.122, yet it is getting points. Seattle's offense ranks 26th in rushing EPA and is down its top two backs. Bosa doubtful and Sigle out are why this isn't higher.
picks.risk: Seattle's 3rd-ranked defense may expose 49ers numbers built mostly against weak defenses, as the 27-7 game at the Rams showed.

picks.label: Purdy passing yards
picks.case: Seattle allows the second-fewest quarterback yards (187.5 a game) and is 2nd in deep EPA allowed. His only game against a top-5 defense produced 205 yards.
picks.risk: Soft underneath coverage could let San Francisco dink its way to yardage.

picks.bet: Purdy under his 2.75-a-game passing TD pace
picks.label: Purdy passing TDs
picks.case: That pace rests on 7 red-zone TDs from 21 attempts and a league-leading 9.7% TD rate, built mostly against bottom-six defenses. Seattle ranks 3rd in defensive EPA and 7th against the pass.
picks.risk: The league's top offense finds three scores anyway if Seattle's passing game turns it into a shootout.

picks.bet: Ravens under their 153.5-a-game team rushing average
picks.label: Team rushing yards
picks.case: Atlanta allows -0.307 EPA per rush, best in the league, and the fewest explosive runs. Baltimore's rushing EPA has been negative two weeks running, guard Gwyn is on IR, and Jackson, reported unlikely with an ankle sprain, takes his own rushing with him.
picks.risk: Baltimore commits to the run anyway with a backup quarterback and piles up volume.

picks.label: Penix passing yards
picks.case: Atlanta passes 10% below expectation and he has averaged only 22.5 attempts even in blowouts. Baltimore ranks 4th against short passes, his main diet, and Atlanta's 2nd-ranked run game faces a 26th-ranked run defense.
picks.risk: If Baltimore's offense keeps pace, Atlanta may have to throw more than usual.

picks.label: Game total
picks.case: Both teams pass less than expected (Baltimore -5.1%, Atlanta -10%) and rank top-10 in time of possession. Atlanta's passing offense is 31st, and Jackson is likely out. The total has already fallen from 45.5 to 43.5, so much of this is priced in.
picks.risk: Atlanta's run game against a 26th-ranked run defense could produce one of its 59- or 69-point-style games.

picks.label: Allen passing yards
picks.case: The Rams allow the fewest passing yards to quarterbacks (167.5) and the fewest explosive passes, and rank first against the deep ball Allen relies on. He averaged just 228.5 yards against the two top-12 defenses he has faced, and DJ Moore is questionable.
picks.risk: Buffalo's 30th-ranked defense turns this into a shootout that forces volume.

picks.label: Game total
picks.case: The number looks set off Buffalo's 31.8 a game, inflated by two weak defenses; against top-12 units it scored 24 and 26. The Rams' defense is 4th in EPA and 1st in explosive passes allowed, and their offense scores only 21.3. Only one Rams game has cleared 54.
picks.risk: Buffalo's defense (30th in EPA, 28th against the pass) could let Stafford light it up in a dome.

picks.label: Allen rushing TD
picks.case: He has scored on the ground in all four games, five times on designed runs, as Buffalo's goal-line option. The Rams' stingy pass defense makes his legs the likelier route, and quarterbacks average 2 total TDs a game against LA.
picks.risk: The Rams' 10th-ranked run defense stuffs him at the goal line, or a running back gets the short score.
